overall: Los Angeles is showing classic marine layer influence this morning, with temperatures sitting at a cool 62.6°F (the running max) as of around 10 PM local time, well before daytime heating begins. Patchy fog, southwest onshore flow at ~11.5 mph, and a relatively high dewpoint of 57.2°F all point to a June Gloom pattern that will cap afternoon warming. No significant warming trend is underway yet, with velocity flat at +0.0°F/hr.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is unusually tight: ECMWF at 68.3°F, HRRR at 68.4°F, and NBM at 67.0°F are all clustered within 1.4°F of each other, lending high confidence to the forecast range. The NWS official forecast of 69°F sits just above the NWP consensus, which is typical given NWS rounding up slightly; no significant outlier model is pulling toward either extreme. Active severe weather alerts (extreme heat, fire weather) are all geographically distant in desert and inland areas and have no bearing on coastal LA temperatures.
max_temp_prediction: Today's TMAX for Los Angeles is highly likely to land in the 67–69°F range, with 68°F as the point estimate. The marine layer will burn off mid-morning per the NWS narrative, allowing limited solar heating into the early-to-mid afternoon before the sea breeze reinforces. The intraday bucket distribution peaks at 68–69°F (13.3%) with meaningful probability spread into the low-to-mid 70s, but the three NWP models converging near 68°F anchors confidence firmly in that zone. Overall confidence is moderately high given tight model agreement, though the residual spread into the 70s reflects uncertainty about the fog burn-off timing and afternoon mixing.
